newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu to form technology policy.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu to form technology policy.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday he planned to set a national policy on science and technology to bring government up to the levels of Israel's vaunted high technology sector.
"You are leading in this sector, but the government is lagging," Netanyahu told the annual convention of the Israeli Information Technology Association.
Netanyahu said he aimed "to bring Israel to a situation where there will be telecommunications and science infrastructure and planning carried out as a national project."
He said a special unit would be formed in the prime minister's office to coordinate technology policy in the government and that he would be forming a ministerial committee.

The committee will lead efforts to improve access to information and services via computers and telecommunications, Netanyahu said. He said he would also seek parliamentary approval for a Freedom of Information Law.
The prime minister said Israel's technology policy also included upgrading the country's telecommunications network and reducing charges.
"This will take some time...but it can be finished in the current government's term," he said. "By the year 2000 the Israeli telecommunications market will be open."
In education, Netanyahu said the government was working with private industry to increase the number of engineers and high tech professionals studying at the university level.

But he emphasised the importance of widening computer education at the elementary school level as well by ensuring classes and access to computers to every child, especially those from low-income families.
Netanyahu said computer education would not be touched by the government's budget cutting. "There will be no cut in the Education Ministry's budget for computers and technology," he said.
